latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 with m2 fixed (seed 24, data_seed 0, 6000 steps), N=128 force peaks at layer 1 with trained R2 0.78436 against a control of 0.63366 (margin 0.151). The paired N=64 arm also peaks at layer 1 and ends at about 0.842 (trajectory value, margin 0.205), so the same-layer N=64 minus N=128 gap is about 0.058. That clears the 0.04 bar, and nearly all of it is in trained R2: the controls are about 0.637 vs 0.634. accel_step is essentially unchanged across the two arms: here layer-4 R2 is 0.96197 vs control 0.75519, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.845, which falls inside [0.60, 0.88]. The N=64 arm reads about 0.966 on its trajectory.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is one seed, and the N=64 reference (run-20261016-055050-9600, paired arm exp-20261016-034512-611f) is only available as rounded trajectory values. Its trajectory R2 field may be the max over layers rather than the layer-1 value, so the gap of about 0.058 could be off by about 0.01. The gap is only measured at matched step, not matched loss. Across checkpoints it stays at about 0.058-0.064 from step 1000 to step 6000, and both arms' force margins are still rising by about 0.002-0.004 per 500 steps. The seed-24 gap of about 0.058 falls between seed 22 (0.108) and seed 23 (0.045) at d128, so it is consistent with a persistent deficit at d128 and adds a third seed in that direction. The verdict would change in either of two cases: the unrounded N=64 layer-1 probes_final R2 comes out below 0.8244, or a reading at matched val_mse_ratio (N=128 ends at 0.015) puts the gap below 0.04. A seed-24 d64 pair is still needed before this seed can say anything about width-driven shrinkage.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 (m2=0.5, data_seed 0, e<=0.5, 6000 steps, seed 24), N=64 force beats its control at layer 1: R2 0.84173 vs control 0.63702, margin 0.205. The paired N=128 arm (run-20261016-060747-3fef) also has force best at layer 1, with step-6000 trajectory R2 0.784 (margin 0.151), so the same-layer layer-1 N=64 minus N=128 trained force R2 gap is about 0.058, above the 0.04 bar. The gap stays at 0.054-0.064 at every checkpoint from step 500 to 6000. accel_step is the same in both arms (layer 4, R2 0.96638 vs about 0.962). This arm's accel_step headroom-normalised margin is 0.861 (control 0.75813), inside the predicted [0.60, 0.88], and its accel_step margin (0.208) is about the same as its force margin (0.205).
latest_findings.confidence_note: There is one seed on one dataset, and this experiment has only one run. The N=128 value comes from the paired arm's rounded trajectory field (its 4th field may be max-over-layers R2 rather than the best-margin-layer R2, see q-20261013-075749-57bb), not from its unrounded probes_final, so the gap of about 0.058 is approximate to about ±0.005. That uncertainty cannot push it below 0.04. The comparison is at matched step and horizon, not matched val_mse_ratio. N=64 reaches val_mse_ratio 0.0035, and the N=128 loss trajectory is not shown here. Both arms are still gaining force at step 6000 (N=128 about +0.003-0.004 per 500 steps, N=64 about +0.002), so the gap may narrow slowly with longer training. Seed 24's d128 gap (0.058) sits between seeds 22 (0.108) and 23 (0.045), so all three d128 seeds now clear 0.04. No d64 run of seed 24 exists, so this run says nothing about how much width shrinks the gap for this seed. The verdict would change if the N=128 probes_final layer-1 R2 came out at 0.80 or above, if a matched-loss read put the gap below 0.04, or if more seeds on data_seed 1 at d128 fell below 0.02.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=256 (N=64, m2 fixed, seed 22, 6000 steps), final force R2 at the best-margin layer (layer 1) is 0.82857 against a control of 0.60495 (margin 0.224 ≥ 0.1). That is within 0.002 of the d_model=128 value (0.82669, layer 4) and within 0.005 of the d_model=64 value (0.8235, layer 1), so N=64 force at its best-margin layer does not rise with width. accel_step is also best at layer 1 with R2 0.92803 against a control of 0.74143, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.72. Distance (R2 0.991) and energy (R2 0.976) are decoded almost perfectly but fail the bar only because their d256 controls are 0.895 and 0.927. Against the paired d256 N=128 arm (run-20261016-042805-cfe4, force best layer 1), the gap can only be estimated from trajectory fields. The best-margin-layer estimate is about 0.03 (0.829 vs about 0.795). The max-over-layers estimate is about 0.07 (0.867 vs 0.795). Both are below the d64 gap of 0.143 and the d128 gap of 0.108.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is one seed (22) on one dataset, and the pre-registered criterion is met. Three things limit confidence. (1) The three widths are compared at different layers: d64 at layer 1, d128 at layer 4, d256 at layer 1. (2) The trajectory's max-over-layers force R2 at step 6000 is 0.867, so some layer other than the best-margin layer 1 (one with a higher control) goes above the 0.86 'width still lifts force' cutoff. Read at the best layer by raw R2 instead of by margin, the result would fall on the expected-if-false side. A fixed-layer readout across d64/d128/d256 could flip the verdict. (3) The paired N=128 gap comes from trajectory fields, not probes_final, so it is an estimate and is not used as evidence here. The verdict would change if per-layer probes_final showed d256 force at some fixed layer at least 0.03 above the same layer at d128, or if a second seed (for example seed 23) moved by more than 0.03. Force was still rising slowly at step 6000 (+0.002 margin from 4500 to 6000).

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=256 (seed 22, m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, N=128, 6000 steps), N=128 trained force R2 at the best-margin layer is 0.79523 at layer 1 (control 0.65467, margin 0.141, headroom-normalised 0.41). That clears the >= 0.74 prediction and is 0.077 above the d128 value (0.718). However, the gap to the paired d256 N=64 arm could not be computed because run-20261016-050924-d030 is still running. accel_step R2 is 0.91127 at layer 1 (control 0.71358, margin 0.198). Its headroom-normalised margin is 0.69: inside [0.60, 0.90] but 0.18 below the d128 seed-22 value of 0.868, so the 'accel_step stays flat' condition fails.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The force part of expected_if_true happened, and by a wide margin. The deciding criterion did not get tested: the best-layer gap (<= 0.085) and the layer-1 same-layer gap (<= 0.10) both need the paired d256 N=64 arm, which has not finished. If that arm lands near the d64/d128 N=64 values (0.8235 at layer 1, 0.82669 at layer 4), the gap would be about 0.03. That would support a capacity bottleneck, but this is an estimate, not a measurement. The accel_step criterion also fails. The normalised margin fell from 0.868 to 0.69, but the trajectory's max-over-layers accel_step R2 is 0.97 while layer 1 reads 0.911, so the drop may come from higher d256 controls (0.714) or from a different best layer rather than a real loss of decodability. The d128 reference's layer would need checking. Controls rise steeply with width: distance control is 0.916 and energy control 0.912, so both fail the 0.1 bar even though trained R2 is 0.97-0.99. The force control (0.655) is also above the d64 values, which is why the hypothesis compares on trained R2. This is a single seed and a single arm. val_mse_ratio is not monotone (0.28 at step 1500, 0.57 at step 2000), but it ends at 0.0127. The verdict becomes supported if the paired arm gives a best-layer gap <= 0.085 and the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact. It becomes refuted only if the paired N=64 arm comes in at >= 0.895, which is implausible given its d64 and d128 values.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 on data_seed 1 (m2 fixed at 0.5, 6000 steps), N=64 force beats its control in both seeds and stays well above the paired N=128 arm. Seed 22: R2 0.86504 vs control 0.6763 (margin 0.189). Seed 23: R2 0.88223 vs control 0.69995 (margin 0.182). Both are at layer 1. Against the N=128 layer-1 values (0.79972 and 0.83083, from f-20261016-043058-4504), the same-layer gaps are +0.065 for seed 22 and +0.051 for seed 23. Those gaps are smaller than the d_model=64 data_seed 1 gaps (about 0.086 and 0.053). At N=64, accel_step (layer 1) is decoded much better than force: R2 0.935 and 0.929 vs controls 0.752 and 0.759, giving headroom-normalised margins of 0.738 and 0.704. But the pre-registered rule that accel_step matches across arms holds only in seed 23 (difference 0.029). In seed 22 the difference is 0.084 against the N=128 value of 0.654.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The force part of expected_if_true was met in both seeds. Both N=64 force margins are at least 0.1, and both N=64 minus N=128 gaps are at least 0.04 at the best-margin layer. Both arms peak at layer 1, so the best-layer gap and the same-layer gap are the same comparison, with no cross-layer pairing. The verdict is inconclusive, not supported, because one pre-registered condition failed: in seed 22 the headroom-normalised accel_step margin differs between arms by 0.084, more than the 0.05 allowed. That difference is also in the opposite direction to a pure force-specific deficit, because N=64 also decodes accel_step better at layer 1. So part of the N=128 shortfall at layer 1 may be a general layer-1 decodability gap, not something specific to force. I could not open the N=128 run files directly. The N=128 values (0.79972, 0.83083, 0.654, 0.675) are taken from f-20261016-043058-4504 and the related open question, not read from those runs' probes_final here. Both runs completed 6000 of 6000 steps. Seed 23's gap (0.051) is close to the 0.04 bar, and there are only two seeds. Things that would change this verdict: (1) N=128 layer-1 values read from the files that differ from the quoted ones; (2) comparing at matched val_mse_ratio, which differs here (N=64 0.0051/0.0029); (3) a third seed, which would show whether the accel_step mismatch in seed 22 is noise. If the accel_step condition is dropped as a secondary control, both seeds support the claim that the force deficit is not a width bottleneck on data_seed 1.

config.expected_if_false: Final layer-1 force R2 <= 0.733 (gap <= 0.02 vs 0.71286), meaning the N=128 deficit closes at matched horizon. A gap between 0.02 and 0.04, or a failed horizon check, is reported as inconclusive.
config.expected_if_true: Final layer-1 force R2 >= 0.753 (gap >= 0.04 vs 0.71286). Force beats its control (margin >= 0.1). Step-12000 layer-1 value within 0.03 of 0.7935. Headroom-normalised accel_step margin in [0.60, 0.85].
config.hypothesis: This is the matched-horizon reference for the seed-23 data_seed 0 ceiling test. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, N=64, seed 23, 4 layers, d_model=64, e in [0, 0.5], best-of-3 controls, 24000 steps. Prediction: the final layer-1 trained force R2 (probes_final, unrounded) stays at least 0.04 above the same-layer 24000-step N=128 seed-23 value of 0.71286 (run-20261014-070746-d284, layer 1). If so, the N=128 deficit is a lower ceiling at matched layer and horizon. The N=64 best-margin layer is reported, and a best layer other than 1 is flagged as cross-layer. Intermediate values are read only as same-layer (layer 1) control plus margin, never from the max-over-layers trajectory field. Horizon check: the step-12000 layer-1 value must be within 0.03 of the 12000-step N=64 seed-23 run's layer-1 value of 0.7935 (run-20261014-043150-2de3). If it is not, the result is reported as horizon-confounded. Both reference run IDs are cited as evidence. Secondary, descriptive only: whether this run's 24000-step endpoint is below the 12000-step endpoint (0.7935), as happened for seed 22 (0.804 vs 0.840).

experiment.expected_if_false: Final layer-1 force R2 <= 0.733 (gap <= 0.02 vs 0.71286), meaning the N=128 deficit closes at matched horizon. A gap between 0.02 and 0.04, or a failed horizon check, is reported as inconclusive.
experiment.expected_if_true: Final layer-1 force R2 >= 0.753 (gap >= 0.04 vs 0.71286). Force beats its control (margin >= 0.1). Step-12000 layer-1 value within 0.03 of 0.7935. Headroom-normalised accel_step margin in [0.60, 0.85].
